verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: fetchStatus now rethrows NotReadyError (meaning "gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet") up to pollCharge, which treats every NotReadyError as "gateway never received it" and calls gw.submit(charge.payload). WHY: submit is explicitly non-idempotent (gateway.ts:3, "every call creates a new charge"), so a merely unsettled charge now gets resubmitted on every tick, creating duplicate charges and double billing. HOW: keep NotReadyError transient handling internal to status/retry (e.g. translate it to a distinct retryable result rather than throwing the same NotReadyError the poller uses as its resubmit signal), or have pollCharge distinguish "not settled" from "not received" before calling submit.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim is technically confirmed by the code. errors.ts:1-2 documents NotReadyError as "the gateway has the charge but has not settled it yet (transient)", while poller.ts:5-8 treats every NotReadyError as "the gateway never received it" and resubmits. status.ts:8-9 now rethrows NotReadyError unchanged (the change at issue), so a merely-unsettled charge propagates to pollCharge, which calls gw.submit (poller.ts:14). gateway.ts:3 explicitly states submit is NOT idempotent (every call creates a new charge), so each tick duplicates the charge. The path is reachable and the root cause is factually accurate. Note this finding is a consequence of applying the earlier round-a-propagate suggestion (which asked to propagate NotReadyError unchanged); it is a different problem (double billing via resubmit) than the earlier one (transient misclassified as terminal), so it is a legitimate revision rather than a repeat. Keep.

WHY: a charge that is merely unsettled yet will cause a brand-new charge to be created on every poll tick, double-billing the customer. HOW: distinguish the two conditions — either throw a dedicated 'not received / resubmittable' error from gw.status and keep NotReadyError as a transient status that pollCharge retries without resubmitting, or make pollCharge stop resubmitting on NotReadyError.

It is NOT a repeat of the PreviousReviewDecisions entry: that entry asked to propagate NotReadyError instead of wrapping it in FailedError; this finding describes the distinct new bug (poller resubmission) that exists precisely BECAUSE that suggestion was applied — a consequence of the earlier fix, which the rules classify as a different problem.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the retry delay added at line 12 (`sleep(200 * attempt)`) is never awaited, so the exponential backoff the change intends to introduce never elapses. WHY: `sleep` (src/sync/sleep.ts:1) returns a Promise that only delays if awaited; calling it bare discards the promise, so the loop immediately proceeds to the next attempt and a failing service is hit `attempts` times back-to-back with no pause. HOW: `await sleep(200 * attempt);` — and since `attempt === attempts` on the last iteration is followed by the throw at line 15, the sleep on that final attempt is pointless, so guard it (e.g. only sleep when `attempt < attempts`) to avoid a dead delay and the misleading 'retrying' log.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The candidate raises the same problem as PreviousReviewDecisions entry round-a-await-sleep, which was posted on this exact PR and marked implemented: sleep() is called without await so the retry backoff never elapses and a failing service is hit attempts times back-to-back. The current code still shows `sleep(200 * attempt);` unawaited (retry.ts:12), i.e. the failure described by the earlier entry — same missing-await, same un-elapsed backoff, same back-to-back retry behavior. Per the repeat rule, this is the same failure already raised on the PR and must be dropped regardless of the entry's outcome or the attempted fix's incompleteness. The extra "guard the final attempt" note is part of the same operation/issue, not a distinct bug.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the await added to fix the missing-backoff problem was applied to log.warn(...) (which returns void) instead of to sleep(200 * attempt), which is still invoked without await on line 12. WHY: awaiting a non-thenable is a no-op, so the backoff still never happens and every retry fires immediately after the previous failure, hammering a failing service with three back-to-back attempts. HOW: move the await to the sleep call: `await sleep(200 * attempt);` (and drop the await from log.warn, or leave it as a plain call). This revises the earlier suggestion whose fix was implemented at the wrong call site.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The code confirms the technical claim: `sleep(200 * attempt)` on line 12 returns a real Promise but is not awaited, so no backoff occurs. However, this is the identical failure already raised by PreviousDecision index 1 (round-a-await-sleep): "sleep(200) without await, so every retry fires immediately after the failure and the backoff never happens." Same operation, same wrong result (no backoff / back-to-back retries). The current finding only names a new cause (await misplaced on log.warn), but the drop rule requires dropping a finding that raises again the problem a prior entry already raised — including when it argues the developer's fix was incomplete or applied at the wrong site. No concrete new evidence shows the area was reworked beyond the prior decision; it is a repeat.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: handleEvent's switch ends with `default: break`, silently discarding every provider event whose `type` is not one of the three handled cases, even though ProviderEvent.type is explicitly widened to `| string` and the cursor is advanced past those events anyway. WHY: any invoice-affecting event type outside the three known literals (a new/renamed provider event such as 'invoice.payment_succeeded', or any string the provider emits) is acknowledged by moving the cursor to pollStartedAt but never applied to InvoicesRepo, so those state changes are permanently lost with no error, log, or alert to surface the gap. HOW: make unrecognized event types observable instead of silently dropped, e.g. log/report the unhandled type in the default branch (and/or add an explicit exhaustive handling for known invoice events) so future event types cannot be swallowed unnoticed.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: ProviderEvent.type is `'invoice.paid' | 'invoice.voided' | 'invoice.payment_failed' | string` (events-client.ts:3), so any arbitrary string is a valid event type. handleEvent's switch (poller.ts:21-33) handles only the three literals and falls through to `default: break`, silently dropping all other types. pollOnce advances the cursor to pollStartedAt for every polled event regardless of handling (poller.ts:17), so an unrecognized invoice-affecting event is permanently acknowledged without being applied to InvoicesRepo, with no log or error. The root cause and failure path are both factually supported by the code. This is distinct from the PreviousReviewDecisions entry (page.hasMore/cursor pagination), which is a different failure in the same function, not the unhandled-event-type drop.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The new comment at poller.ts:15-16 and PAGE_SIZE=500 assert that page.hasMore is never true, but events-client.ts:16 documents that the provider caps limit at 100 regardless of the requested value, so hasMore can be true and the single page read here is not exhaustive. WHY: The false invariant is used to justify advancing the cursor to pollStartedAt, so when more than 100 events exist in the window the events beyond the first 100 are silently never processed and the cursor skips past them. HOW: Do not rely on the limit; loop on the returned pagination fields (read page.nextCursor and keep calling listEvents with cursor until page.hasMore is false) before setting the cursor, and remove/correct the false comment.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The technical claim is factually supported (events-client.ts:16 confirms the 100-event cap, so hasMore can be true). But this is the same problem already raised by PreviousDecision index 1 (round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only), marked "implemented": reading only the first page then advancing the cursor to pollStartedAt, losing events beyond the first 100 in the same operation. The current diff shows the identical first-page-only read with no evidence the applied change was reverted. This is a repeat of an already-posted finding, so it must be dropped per the repeat rule.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: PAGE_SIZE is raised to 500 and the comment claims page.hasMore is never true, but the EventsClient contract states the provider caps limit at 100 ('a larger limit still returns at most 100 events'), so any window with more than 100 events still returns hasMore=true and the events beyond the first 100 are never read. WHY: because the cursor is then advanced to pollStartedAt, those invoice.paid/voided/payment_failed events are skipped permanently and the corresponding invoices never get marked paid/voided/past-due. HOW: loop on the cursor instead of assuming one page suffices — after processing a page, if page.hasMore and page.nextCursor is set, call listEvents again with cursor: page.nextCursor until hasMore is false, then advance the cursor to pollStartedAt.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The finding describes the exact same failure already raised in PreviousDecision index 1 (round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only): pollOnce reads a single page and then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt, so events beyond the first page are permanently lost. That entry is marked implemented, and the current code still exhibits the same data-loss failure. Per the rules, re-raising the problem a PreviousReviewDecisions entry already raised is a repeat and must be dropped, regardless of the new cause named (PAGE_SIZE=500 vs 100) or the incompleteness of the fix. This is the same wrong result/loss in the same operation, not a distinct bug.

WHY: Ref.Final is false while the build is still uploading (live.go:15-16), so an all-projects sweep deletes the blobs of in-flight builds; when such a build finalizes its ref points at a blob that no longer exists — the same data-loss failure the sibling ByProject branch explicitly guards against ('Non-final refs belong to builds still uploading: their blobs stay'). verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: In the new scope.All branch, liveDigests only marks a digest live when r.Final is true, so non-final (still-uploading) refs are omitted from the live set. WHY: Sweep uses this map to delete every blob not present in it, so an all-projects sweep deletes the blobs of builds that are still uploading; when such a build finalizes, its ref points at a blob that no longer exists (data loss). The sibling ByProject branch (lines 45-48) deliberately marks every ref live with the comment "Non-final refs belong to builds still uploading: their blobs stay" — this new branch contradicts that contract. HOW: drop the Final check and mark every ref digest as live, matching the ByProject branch: `for _, r := range refs { live[r.Digest] = true }`.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: When scope.All is set, blobs.List(ctx, "") returns every blob digest for the whole instance into a single in-memory slice, and Sweep then issues one blobs.Delete round-trip per unreferenced blob in an unbounded loop (sweep.go:21-34). WHY: the all-projects scope is exactly the case with the largest data volume — a full instance with millions of blobs materializes the entire digest list at once and performs millions of sequential Delete calls, causing memory blowup and a multi-minute/blocking sweep; the RefStore.All call in liveDigests (live.go:28) similarly loads every ref for every project into one map. HOW: paginate/stream the listing (e.g. List with a page/continuation token or a channel-based iterator) and delete in batches rather than loading everything and deleting one digest at a time.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The code confirms the claim exactly: `blobs.List(ctx, "")` (sweep.go:21) returns a full `[]string` of every blob digest for the whole instance into memory, and the loop at sweep.go:26-34 issues one sequential `blobs.Delete` per unreferenced digest with no pagination or batching. The `BlobStore` interface (sweep.go:5-9) exposes only `List`/`Delete` with no page/continuation token, so there is no upstream guard bounding volume. `liveDigests` (live.go:26-38) similarly materializes all refs via `store.All`. The all-projects scope is the largest-volume case, so the described memory blowup and long blocking sweep are real consequences of the code as written, not a style nit. The prior streaming decision (round-a-other-17/-2) concerns `src/reports/export.ts`, a different operation, so this is not a repeat. Cannot refute.
